newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary o/n rate down, repo cut not excluded - dealer.
newsitem.headline: Hungary o/n rate down, repo cut not excluded - dealer.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interest rates rose slightly on Tuesday as liquidity in the banking system tightened due to repo cut expectations and other factors.
The overnight rates finished at between 21 and 21.25 percent, up from Monday's closing of 20.875 percent. Some dealers said the rise was surprising.
"Everybody expected the rates to remain down," said Istvan Zsoter of Takarekbank.
But another dealer said the market found its balance at the current levels, and the overnight and tomnext rates were not likely to change much on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"The market found healthy levels between 21 and 21.25 percent," said Balazs Varga of Inter-Europa Bank. "Demand and supply is balanced now."
However, dealers agreed that the market's liquidity tightened on Tuesday.
They said April 20 tax-payments draw funds out of the market and money may have flowed in the central bank's reverse repo facilities due to market talks about potential repo rate cuts.
The National Bank of Hungary cooled repo rate cut expectations one month ago when it raised the rate of its six-month deposit facility.
Dealers said rate cut expectations began to spread again, but they could not identify the source of these market talks.
However, they added that these expectations were not very strong.
"I do not exclude the possibility (of repo cuts)," said Varga. "But the expectation does not saturate what I do every day."
